registration.rule: This protocol is registered when it is merged into main. No Study 3 outcome may exist at that moment: no mutant, and no Study 2 fault on a new learner, has been executed against any check or alarm; the margin simulation has not been run; neither predictability estimator has been run on a scorecard cell; no scorecard of a Part 6 model has been made, other than scorecards of the two built-in baselines at other seeds (the published ones, and those of the last-value forecaster made when the scorecard's interval was measured). Every computation made before registration is listed under pilots_before_registration.
registration.after_merge: Three later commits may change this file, each one value only. The first, right after the merge, writes registered_on and merge_commit and sets status to 'registered'. The second adds the generated mutant sources and their manifest and writes the manifest's SHA-256 into part_1_generated_mutants.sources.manifest.sha256. The third writes the Chronos revision into part_6_zoo.models. Nothing else in this file changes after the merge.

tolerances.justification: The Study 2 tolerances, unchanged, so that deterministic verdicts are comparable with the four Study 2 bugs.

monte_carlo_rank_checks.rule: timegym.diagnostics.rank_alarm: p = (1 + number of calibration values >= observed) / (B + 1); FAIL when p <= alpha.
monte_carlo_rank_checks.justification: With B = 239, p-values are multiples of 1/240 and the four Holm thresholds for a family of four at 0.05 are attained exactly: 3/240 = 0.0125, 4/240 = 0.05/3, 6/240 = 0.025, 12/240 = 0.05 (checked in floating point).

split_calibration_alarms.rule: experiments.run_supplement.conformal_threshold on 239 clean calibration scores per condition and learner; per-case alarm when the evaluation score strictly exceeds the threshold (rank ceil(240 x 0.95) = 228), equivalently rank_alarm p <= alpha.
split_calibration_alarms.justification: The same resolution as the Monte Carlo checks, so that the alpha grid of the detection curves is the set of attainable levels k/240.

evaluation_cases_per_condition.precision_target: Wilson 95% interval (timegym.statistics.wilson_interval) with half-width at most 10 percentage points at every possible count.
evaluation_cases_per_condition.arithmetic: The Wilson half-width is largest at a rate of 1/2, where it equals z sqrt(1/(4n) + z^2/(4n^2)) / (1 + z^2/n) with z = 1.95996. n = 92 gives 0.1001; n = 93 gives 0.0996 (largest over all counts 0 to 93); every n from 93 to 133 stays below 0.10. The Wald formula z^2/(4 x 0.1^2) = 96.04 gives 96 or 97; it is not the Wilson interval the protocol uses.
evaluation_cases_per_condition.applies_to: Parts 1 and 2 (evaluation cases per condition) and Part 3 (independent suites).

shared.per_mutant_deterministic_rule: A deterministic check (output checks, scalar shift, per-target shift, second implementation) catches a mutant in a condition when it alarms on at least one of the evaluated cases of that condition. This rule is valid only if the clean pipeline raises no alarm of that check on any calibration or evaluation case of that condition and learner; the run verifies this. If the clean pipeline alarms on any case, the check is reported as not deterministic for that condition and learner, with the clean alarm count, and no caught verdict of that check is given there; nothing is dropped.

per_mutant_statistical_rule.split_calibration_alarms: For the calibrated loss alarm and the answer-key alarm, with m evaluated cases of a mutant in a condition (shared.evaluated_cases) and x per-case alarms: p = P(X >= x) for X ~ BetaBinomial(m, a = 240 - 228 = 12, b = 228), computed with scipy.stats.betabinom. Caught when Holm (experiments.run_supplement.holm_rejections) at 0.05 rejects within the family of all non-equivalent mutants of the same source and learner in that condition.
per_mutant_statistical_rule.assumption: Under the null that the mutant's evaluation scores and the 239 clean calibration scores of the condition are independent and identically distributed (a mutant that changes nothing the score sees), the number of evaluation scores above the k-th calibration order statistic follows BetaBinomial(m, n + 1 - k, k), whatever the score distribution, when ties have probability zero; ties only lower the count. The p-value is valid marginally over the calibration draw. All mutants of a condition share one calibration sample, so their p-values are positively dependent; Holm needs no independence. The exact binomial test against alpha would assume a conditional alarm probability of exactly alpha given the frozen calibration sample, which is false: that probability is Beta(12, 228) distributed with standard deviation 0.014, and the binomial tail understates the true one (for 93 cases, P(X >= 10) is 0.0179 binomial against 0.0388 beta-binomial).
per_mutant_statistical_rule.calibrated_shift_check: For the calibrated shift check of Part 2 every case draws its own 39 refits, so per-case FAILs are independent with probability exactly 2/40 = 0.05 under the null: an exact binomial test of x FAILs among the m cases that the check decided (PASS or FAIL; a case where the check returns ERROR is counted in its own column and left out of m) against 0.05 (scipy.stats.binom), with Holm as above.
per_mutant_statistical_rule.paired_check: One-sided sign-flip test of the mean paired difference d_i = mse(answer key, mutant forecast) - mse(answer key, clean forecast) over the evaluated cases: experiments.run_addendum.sign_flip_pvalue(d, 9999, numpy.random.default_rng([7600000, len(d)])), with Holm as above. A Holm family must not exceed 500 members, because the smallest attainable p-value is 1/10000 and the first Holm threshold is 0.05/m; the cap of 400 generated mutants guarantees this.
per_mutant_statistical_rule.family_sizes: The Holm families of the sources differ in size (4 Study 2 bugs, 16 catalogue mutants, up to 400 generic mutants), so one alarm count is not one verdict: among 93 cases a calibrated alarm needs 10 alarms unadjusted, 12 in a family of 4, 14 in a family of 16 and 18 in a family of 400. The unadjusted decision (p <= 0.05) is reported beside every Holm decision, and sources are compared on the detection curves and on per-case alarm rates, not on counts of Holm rejections.
per_mutant_statistical_rule.holm_families: A family holds the non-equivalent sources of one kind (generated by Cosmic Ray, catalogue, Study 2 bugs) for one learner, check and condition. A source without an evaluated case in the condition has no p-value there and is left out; the size of the family actually used is reported with every decision. A source that carries labels of several kinds (a catalogue operator whose source is also a Study 2 bug, or also a generated mutant) belongs to the family and to the funnel of each of its kinds.

shared.evaluated_cases: The calibrated alarms and the paired check use the cases where the source returned a forecast that passes the output checks (Forecast.validate(case.task) reports nothing and every point is finite). The other completed cases are counted as unevaluable; cases where the source raised, and cases not finished within the time limit, have their own columns. The deterministic checks other than the output checks run on every case where the source returned a forecast.
shared.holm: experiments.run_supplement.holm_rejections, the step-down procedure of protocols 2.0 and 2.2.
shared.uncertainty: Wilson 95% intervals (timegym.statistics.wilson_interval) for every rate: over cases for case-level rates, over suites for suite-level rates, over repetitions for Part 4, and over mutants for funnel proportions (descriptive of the generated set, not of a population of real faults). Nothing is dropped after the run: every exception, timeout, unsupported or unevaluable case is counted and reported in its own column.
shared.multiplicity: Holm families are declared per part. No multiplicity claim spans parts, mutant sources, learners, checks or conditions unless stated.
shared.unit_of_work: One unit is one source (the clean subject, a Study 2 bug or a mutant) with one learner in one condition. Each unit runs in a fresh Python process that imports its source once. Before any other work the unit fits and forecasts once on the condition's warm-up context, the equivalence input i = 0, and discards the result; the clean subject gets the same warm-up. The unit then takes its cases in increasing seed order (the 8 equivalence inputs, the calibration cases for the clean subject, evaluation cases) and, within a case, the fixed order forecast, output checks, scalar shift check, per-target shift check, second implementation, calibrated shift check. The equivalence verdict of a source needs all six conditions, so a source runs as two units per condition: a screen unit (warm-up fit and the 8 equivalence inputs) and, once it is classified, an evaluation unit that repeats the warm-up fit and the 8 equivalence inputs before the evaluation cases, so that the state of its process follows the same order. Units may run in parallel; no unit reads the state of another, so results do not depend on the number of workers.

The entries of namespaces describe the same seeds in words.

case_seed_blocks.format: name: [base, stride, blocks, count]; the seeds of a namespace are base + stride * b + i for b < blocks and i < count. The runners take every case seed from this table.

part_1_generated_mutants.question: Which checks catch generated mutants of a lag-regression pipeline that pass the output checks, and how do generated mutants compare with the four hand-placed Study 2 bugs?

subject.rule: The subject is written for this study on the model of the clean branch of experiments/model_faults.LagRidgeImplementation, committed and hashed (frozen_files_sha256) before any mutant is generated, and never edited afterwards; the second implementation, the catalogue and the learners are frozen with it. It contains no argument validation, so that generated mutants act on the forecasting computation.

required_structure.constants: No module-level constants other than imports; window, period and scaling are constructor arguments.
functions: training_matrix(values, window, period) -> (features, targets): start = max(window, period); for every row t in range(start, len(values)) the feature row is the flattened lag block values[t - window:t] (site T-lag) followed by the seasonal lag values[t - period] (site T-season); targets = values[start:] (site T-target).
prediction_row(history, window, period) -> array of shape (1, features): the flattened lag block history[-window:] (site P-lag) followed by history[-period] (site P-season).
fit_scaler(array) -> (center, scale): column means and population standard deviations, with a zero scale replaced by 1.
invert_scaler(array, center, scale) -> array * scale + center.
required_structure.class: SubjectForecaster(make_regressor, window=6, period=12, scaling='global') with clone_unfitted(), fit(context) and predict(future_index), usable as Pipeline(SubjectForecaster(...)). fit: values = context as float array; features, targets = training_matrix(...); when scaling is 'global', the feature and target scalers are fitted with fit_scaler (sites S-x and S-y) and applied with apply_scaler; regressor = make_regressor().fit(features, targets). predict: a loop for step in range(len(future_index)) (site H) builds prediction_row from the current history, scales it, calls regressor.predict, applies invert_scaler with the target scaler when scaling is 'global' (site I), appends the value to the list of points, and appends it to the history (site R); it returns timegym.Forecast(index=future_index.copy(), point=points, target_names=context columns).
required_structure.site_markers: Each site carries a trailing comment '# site: <name>' on its line, with the names above, so that the catalogue transformer finds exactly one node per site and fails loudly when the expected pattern is absent.

configuration.justification: Window and penalty of Study 2; period 12 is the seasonal period of the seasonal_scales condition and gives the seasonal-period operator something to change in every condition (start = 12 rows, at most 15% of the shortest context of 80).

subject.second_implementation: experiments/study3_reference.py: an independent NumPy implementation of the same forecaster (lag columns built as one block per lag, seasonal column, augmented normal equations with an unpenalized intercept, solved in original target units, recursive forecasting), receiving neither the future nor generator parameters, as normal_equation_forecast in protocol 2.0. Used for Ridge only. It is written before any mutant is generated and is frozen with the subject.

part_1_generated_mutants.conditions: The six conditions of protocol 2.0 model_study.conditions, unchanged and in the order of condition_ids.

cosmic_ray.operators: All operators that 'cosmic-ray operators' lists in that version (213 names in 16 families: ReplaceBinaryOperator, ReplaceComparisonOperator, ReplaceUnaryOperator, AddNot, ReplaceTrueWithFalse, ReplaceFalseWithTrue, ReplaceAndWithOr, ReplaceOrWithAnd, ReplaceBreakWithContinue, ReplaceContinueWithBreak, ExceptionReplacer, NumberReplacer, RemoveDecorator, ZeroIterationForLoop, VariableReplacer, VariableInserter). VariableReplacer and VariableInserter take arguments that 'cosmic-ray init' reads from its configuration; with none, as here, init makes no mutant from them, so the generated mutants come from the other 14 families. The full list, and the operators that made no mutant for this reason, are stored with the manifest.
cosmic_ray.generation: experiments/study3_generate.py, run in the Cosmic Ray environment: it enumerates the (operator, occurrence) pairs of experiments/study3_subject.py as 'cosmic-ray init' does (on a toy module its list equals init's in content, order and positions; pilots test-suite-runs) and writes each mutated source with cosmic_ray.mutating.mutate_code, then adds the catalogue sources and the Study 2 bug sources. No Cosmic Ray test command is used: Cosmic Ray only generates sources, and the Study 3 harness executes them. The generic mutants of this protocol are the distinct generated sources that are not also a catalogue source or a Study 2 bug source.
cosmic_ray.sampling_rule: If more than 400 generic mutants are generated, all catalogue sources and Study 2 bug sources are run and a sample of 400 generic mutants is drawn without replacement, stratified by operator family. Families are taken in the order of their first mutant in the manifest. A family of size s among a total of t first receives min(s, max(1, floor(400 s / t + 0.5))) places; while the places do not sum to 400, one place is added to the family, among those not yet full, whose quota 400 s / t exceeds its places by most, or removed from the family, among those with more than one place, whose places exceed its quota by most, the earlier family winning a tie. One numpy.random.default_rng(7500000) then draws a permutation of each family in turn, and the family's first places in its permutation are taken. If 400 or fewer are generated, all are run.
cosmic_ray.cap_justification: The pilot counted 30 mutants on the 34-line clean branch of the Study 2 pipeline and 348 on the whole 132-line fixture file; the subject should fall between. 400 keeps every Holm family of the paired check below 500 members (shared.per_mutant_statistical_rule.paired_check) and the run within a few CPU-hours (runtime_estimate_cpu_hours).

manifest.rule: Written by experiments/study3_generate.py with one file per distinct source (sources/<SHA-256>.py): the tool version and its environment, the operator list, the subject's digest, and per source its labels (kind, operator, family, occurrence or site, enclosing definition) and SHA-256. Sources that are identical after ast.unparse(ast.parse(source)) are one source with several labels. The commit that adds these files writes the manifest's SHA-256 into sha256; Parts 1 and 2 refuse to start without it, refuse a source file whose digest differs from the manifest, and refuse a manifest not made from the frozen subject.

catalogue.implementation: experiments/study3_catalogue.py, standard library only: each operator finds its site by the trailing '# site: <name>' comment, takes the one statement that starts on that line, checks that it has exactly the expected form and replaces it; any other form is an error. Each operator produces exactly one mutant source, written by ast.unparse, so mutant sources carry no comments. Two edits touch a line that is not a site: horizon_index_off_by_one also changes the returned points to points[1:], and the Study 2 bug swap_recursive_targets is placed after the statement value = output[0]; both are found by their exact text inside predict. The two scaler-reuse operators keep the first call's statistics in a module-level dictionary of the mutant source.
catalogue.kinds: Ten kinds of time-series bug, written as 16 operators: lag window off by one (3), lag order reversed (2), recursion state not updated (1), horizon index off by one (1), target and feature columns swapped (2: the target columns in training, the series columns of the features at prediction), scaler fitted once and reused across contexts (2), inverse transform skipped (1) or applied twice (1), seasonal period off by one (2), training rows dropped from the wrong end (1).

operators.definition: In training_matrix the lag block values[t - window:t] becomes values[t - window - 1:t - 1], so every training row uses lags 2 to window + 1 while prediction uses lags 1 to window.
In prediction_row the lag block history[-window:] becomes history[-window - 1:-1], so prediction uses lags 2 to window + 1 while training used lags 1 to window.

In training_matrix the lag block values[t - window:t] becomes values[t - window + 1:t + 1], so every training row holds its own target as its newest lag (look-ahead within the context), while prediction uses lags 1 to window.
In training_matrix the lag block values[t - window:t] becomes values[t - window:t][::-1], so training rows list the lags newest first while prediction rows list them oldest first.
In prediction_row the lag block history[-window:] becomes history[-window:][::-1], so prediction rows list the lags newest first while training rows list them oldest first.
The statement that appends the forecast value to the history in predict is removed, so every step after the first is computed from the observed context alone.
The loop in predict runs range(len(future_index) + 1) and the returned points are points[1:], so the value reported for step h is the recursive forecast for step h + 1.

In training_matrix targets = values[start:] becomes values[start:][:, ::-1], so each output column is fitted against the other series' label while the feature blocks keep their order. For a regressor that fits each target separately (Ridge, one gradient-boosting model per target) its forecasts equal those of the Study 2 bug swap_recursive_targets up to rounding, although the sources differ; both are run and reported.
In prediction_row the lag block history[-window:] becomes history[-window:][:, ::-1], so at prediction each series' lags sit in the feature columns that held the other series' lags in training.

The call fit_scaler(features) in fit is replaced by a call that keeps the center and scale of its first call in the module and returns them on every later call, so every later context is standardized with the statistics of the first. With the warm-up fit of shared.unit_of_work, these are the statistics of the condition's warm-up context.

The call fit_scaler(targets) in fit is replaced by a call that keeps the center and scale of its first call in the module and returns them on every later call, so every later forecast is inverted with the statistics of the first. With the warm-up fit of shared.unit_of_work, these are the statistics of the condition's warm-up context.
The call invert_scaler(output, ...) in predict is replaced by output, so forecasts and the recursive history stay in standardized units.
The call invert_scaler(output, ...) in predict is replaced by invert_scaler(invert_scaler(output, ...), ...) with the same scaler, so the inverse transform is applied twice.

In training_matrix the seasonal lag values[t - period] becomes values[t - period - 1], so training uses lag period + 1 (and the first row reads values[-1], the last context value) while prediction uses lag period.
In prediction_row the seasonal lag history[-period] becomes history[-period - 1], so prediction uses lag period + 1 while training used lag period.

In training_matrix targets = values[start:] becomes values[:len(values) - start], so the rows without a full lag history are removed from the end of the targets instead of the beginning and every feature row is paired with the target start steps earlier. With window 6 and period 12, start equals the period, so each row's target is its own seasonal-lag feature.

catalogue.leakage: No operator can leak the evaluation future: the pipeline receives only the context and the future index, never future values, so no edit of its source can read them. Look-ahead within the context can be written, and lag_window_includes_target_training is that operator; seasonal_period_off_by_one_training also produces it, on its first training row only.

study2_bugs.purpose: The four Study 2 bugs re-expressed on the subject, run through the same funnel, so that generated mutants and hand-placed bugs are compared on one pipeline.

bugs.definition: After value = output[0] in predict, value = value[::-1].copy(), so the two target columns are exchanged in the returned points and in the recursive history while the labels keep their order.

study2_bugs.deduplication: Mutant sources that are identical after ast.unparse(ast.parse(source)) are executed once and reported under every label that produced them; the number of duplicates is reported per source.

stages: caught by the scalar shift check
caught by the per-target shift check
caught by the calibrated loss alarm
funnel.runnable: The source compiles, the module imports, and the mutant returns a forecast for at least one of the N fixed inputs within the time limit. Otherwise it is not runnable, with the reason recorded (syntax error, import error, exception on every input, timeout, or a process that ended without finishing).

equivalence.inputs: The first 4 equivalence-input seeds of each of the six conditions (seeds namespace equivalence_inputs, i = 0-3), each screened inside its condition's screen unit after the warm-up fit (shared.unit_of_work). The screen unit forecasts all 8 inputs of its condition, so that N = 6, 24 and 48 are read from one run (inputs_per_condition gives the inputs per condition behind each N).
equivalence.rule: A runnable mutant is equivalent when on every one of the N inputs it returns a forecast whose index and target names equal the clean forecast's, whose point array has the clean shape and is finite, and whose points satisfy numpy.allclose(mutant, clean, atol=1e-8, rtol=1e-7); for a learner with a free training seed both use identical seed streams. An exception on any input where the clean pipeline returns a forecast makes the mutant not equivalent.
equivalence.N_justification: Four inputs in each condition cover both targets, the seasonal condition, the shortest context (80) and the random walk; the screen costs about 0.1 s per mutant with Ridge.
equivalence.sensitivity: Registered: the equivalence classification is also computed at N = 6 (i = 0) and N = 48 (i = 0-7) and both are reported beside N = 24. In addition, for every mutant classified equivalent at N = 24, forecasts (only) are computed on all evaluation cases and the number of mutants that differ from the clean forecast on at least one evaluation case is reported as screen misses; such mutants stay in the equivalent stage of the primary funnel.

time_limit.rule: Per unit (a source with a learner in a condition): the larger of 120 s and 20 times the wall time of the clean unit of that learner and condition for the same stages, including the start of its process and its warm-up fit. A unit that only forecasts (a screen unit, or the evaluation unit of an equivalent source) is measured against the clean unit's forecast times. A unit stopped at its limit keeps every case it finished; the others are reported as not evaluated, case by case.

funnel.proportions: Runnable over the sources run; equivalent and not equivalent over the runnable sources; caught by a check over the sources that are not equivalent.

output_checks.alarm: Forecast.validate(case.task) returns a violation, the point array is not finite, or the mutant raises on the case (raised cases are also reported in their own column). A violation does not stop the run.

scalar_shift.alarm: timegym.checks.check_shift_equivariance with shift 10.0 and the shared tolerances returns FAIL or ERROR (ERROR counts are reported separately).

per_target_shift.alarm: experiments.model_faults.target_shift_agreement with shifts [7.0, -11.0] and the shared tolerances raises an alarm. An exception raised while the check refits on a shifted context counts as an alarm and is reported with its error.

second_implementation.alarm: experiments.model_faults.point_agreement between the mutant forecast and experiments/study3_reference.py on the same context raises an alarm; a forecast with a point that is not finite alarms. Ridge only.

loss_alarm.calibration: The 239 clean calibration cases of the condition, with the clean subject and the same learner.

answer_key_alarm.score: timegym.metrics.mse(case.reference.mean, forecast.point), the alarm of protocol 2.1

paired_check.rule: shared.per_mutant_statistical_rule.paired_check, against the clean subject on the same evaluation cases.

part_1_generated_mutants.caught: Per mutant, check and condition, as defined in shared.per_mutant_deterministic_rule and shared.per_mutant_statistical_rule, with the unadjusted decision beside each Holm decision. A mutant is reported as caught by a check in at least one condition as a descriptive count, with no multiplicity claim across the six conditions.

curves.detection_rate: At each level, per source kind and condition and pooled over conditions: the alarm rate of each non-equivalent mutant among its evaluated cases (pooled over conditions first, for the pooled curve), averaged over the mutants with at least one evaluated case, so that each mutant weighs the same.
curves.false_alarm_rate: At each level: alarms of the clean subject among its 93 evaluation cases per condition (558 pooled).
curves.interval: Wilson 95% at the levels 3/240, 6/240, 12/240 and 24/240, taken over all (mutant, evaluated case) pairs without weights, because the equally weighted rate is not a binomial proportion; curves are drawn without intervals.

reported: The funnel per source (Cosmic Ray, catalogue, Study 2 bugs) and learner, with counts and Wilson intervals.
Per mutant: operator, site or occurrence, stage, and per condition the alarm counts of every check, the p-values, Holm decisions and the number of evaluated cases.
The clean pipeline's alarm counts for every check, condition and learner.
The equivalence sensitivity at N = 6, 24 and 48 and the screen misses.

results.json holds, per source and condition, counts, p-values and decisions, and the clean calibration scores; the per-case ranks and paired differences behind them are recomputed by rerunning and are not stored.

part_2_learners.question: Do the checks transfer to learners beyond Ridge once each learner's shift relation is classified on the clean pipeline first?

hgb.regressor: sklearn.multioutput.MultiOutputRegressor(sklearn.ensemble.HistGradientBoostingRegressor()) with scikit-learn 1.9.1 defaults (max_iter 100, learning_rate 0.1, max_leaf_nodes 31, min_samples_leaf 20; early stopping is off below 10000 rows), one model per target.
hgb.justification: On raw lags the relation is the learner's own property: the bins follow the order of the feature values and the baseline moves with the targets. With global scaling any deterministic regressor would be exact, because the standardized inputs do not change under a shift. The pilot passed 12 of 12 clean cases on raw lags (pilots raw-lag-public-check).

mlp_window_standardized.regressor: experiments/study3_learners.WindowStandardizedMLP: for each row, the window lags and the seasonal lag of each target series are standardized by the mean and population standard deviation of that series' window lags in the row (the seasonal lag does not enter these statistics; a zero sd is replaced by 1), the target by the same mean and sd; sklearn.neural_network.MLPRegressor(hidden_layer_sizes=(32,), max_iter=500) with all other parameters at their defaults and random_state drawn from the free seed stream at every fit; outputs are mapped back with the row's mean and sd.

mlp_raw.regressor: MLPRegressor(hidden_layer_sizes=(32,), max_iter=500) on the raw lag features and raw targets, random_state from the free seed stream at every fit.

learners.scaling: All three learners use the subject with scaling 'none'. The four catalogue operators at the scaler sites (S-x, S-y and both at I) and the Study 2 bug omit_inverse_target_scaling change nothing there and are expected to be classed as equivalent; they are screened and reported like every other source.
learners.hyperparameter_justification: Fixed from the clean timing pilot only (0.06 s, 0.11 s and 0.06 s per fit and forecast). ConvergenceWarnings are counted and reported, not treated as failures; the pilot saw them on every window-standardized fit at max_iter 500.

part_2_learners.note_on_tree_models: Random forests, extra trees, single trees and GradientBoostingRegressor failed the public check on clean raw-lag pipelines in the pilot (pilots raw-lag-public-check), so they are not used: where two splits separate the training rows equally well, rounding decides between them after the shift. Histogram gradient boosting bins features by their order, which a shift does not change.

shift_classification.cases: 16 per condition (96), seeds namespace classification_cases, for the Ridge subject of Part 1 (global scaling, as a control) and the three learners.
rule: exact: the public check_shift_equivariance (shift 10.0, shared tolerances) returns PASS on every one of the 96 classification cases. An ERROR of the public check counts as not PASS.

Otherwise the calibrated shift check runs on the 96 classification cases. in distribution: the number of FAILs x among the m cases that the check decided satisfies P(Binomial(m, 0.05) >= x) > 0.05; with m = 96 that is x <= 9. not applicable: otherwise (x >= 10 at m = 96, P = 0.022). A case where the calibrated check returns ERROR is counted and left out of m.
A learner classified not applicable is reported as its own outcome; it is not a FAIL of any bug.
shift_classification.pilot_evidence: In the 12-case pilots, histogram gradient boosting on raw lags passed the public check on every case; the window-standardized perceptron failed it on every case with a free seed and passed on every case with a fixed seed, so its class comes from the free seed, not from the standardization; the perceptron on raw lags failed on every case.
shift_classification.seeds: Each check of the classification starts the case's training seed stream afresh, so the public check and the calibrated check see the same first fit.

calibrated_shift_check.location: experiments/study3_shift.py; not added to the package.
calibrated_shift_check.distance: dist(a, b) = mean over horizon steps and targets of (a - b)^2.
calibrated_shift_check.draw_order: On each case, from the learner's free seed stream: the forecast fit R on the context (seed draw 1, also the forecast evaluated by every other check), 39 refits F_1..F_39 on the context (draws 2-40), and one fit G on context + 10 (draw 41).
calibrated_shift_check.rule: Calibration values dist(R, F_j), j = 1-39; observed dist(R, G - 10); rank_alarm(observed, calibration, alpha=0.05). p-values are multiples of 1/40; FAIL when at most one calibration distance is >= the observed one.
calibrated_shift_check.tolerance: If G - 10 equals R within the shared tolerances (numpy.allclose(G - 10, R, atol=1e-8, rtol=1e-7)), the check returns PASS whatever the ranks, and the rank p-value is still recorded. A forecast that does not depend on the training seed (a mutant can produce one) has 39 calibration distances of exactly zero, so rounding in G - 10 alone would otherwise rank above them and FAIL. The rule can only turn a FAIL into a PASS, so the bound on the FAIL probability stands.
calibrated_shift_check.validity: If the law of G - 10 given the context equals the law of a refit on the context, and seeds are independent draws, then G - 10, F_1, ..., F_39 are exchangeable given R and the FAIL probability is at most 0.05 on every case.
calibrated_shift_check.errors: An exception in any of the 41 fits, or a refit without a finite point forecast of R's shape, gives ERROR; ERRORs are counted per source and condition and are not FAILs.
calibrated_shift_check.cases: The check runs on the evaluation cases, not on the clean calibration cases: its clean false-alarm rate is the FAIL rate of the clean subject on its 93 evaluation cases per condition (558 pooled).

checks_by_class.note: The second implementation exists only for Ridge.

bugs.study2: The four Study 2 bugs of Part 1, on each learner.
bugs.catalogue: All 16 catalogue mutants of Part 1, on each learner.
bugs.generic: 12 Cosmic Ray mutants per learner, taken from every generic mutant of the manifest (not from the Part 1 sample). One numpy.random.default_rng(7500001) first permutes the operator families (listed in the order of their first mutant in the manifest) and then, in that permuted order, the mutants of each family; the order takes one mutant from each family in turn until none is left. The first 12 in that order that are runnable and not equivalent for the learner are taken. Mutants are screened in that order in batches of max(12, number of workers), so a few beyond the twelfth taken may be screened; every screened mutant is reported. Selection uses only the order and the screens, never a check outcome.
bugs.size_justification: Per non-equivalent source over the 558 evaluation cases: about 100 s for gradient boosting, 35 s for the raw perceptron and 2500 s for the window-standardized perceptron, whose calibrated shift check needs 41 fits per case. Each learner receives 29 distinct sources (4 Study 2 bugs, 16 catalogue mutants and 12 generic mutants, three Study 2 bugs sharing their source with a catalogue mutant), of which the four at the scaler sites are expected to be equivalent: about 25 evaluated sources. The runner's --plan, which assumes that all 29 are evaluated, gives at most about 24 CPU-hours in all.

part_2_learners.cases: The Part 1 calibration (239) and evaluation (93) seeds per condition, with each learner's own clean calibration.
part_2_learners.caught: As in Part 1, per learner; Holm families are per learner, source kind, check and condition.
reported: The classification table: per learner, public-check PASS count, calibrated-check FAIL count and binomial p-value, class.
The clean alarm counts of every check per learner and condition, including the calibrated shift check's clean false-alarm rate with its Wilson interval.

part_3_suite_questions.question: Answer separately, with one declared method each, whether a covariance suite contains any failure and which condition failed.
part_3_suite_questions.design: The covariance study of protocol 2.0, repeated with n_calibration = 239 and new seeds; conditions, variants and every other setting unchanged.
part_3_suite_questions.prior_evidence: Protocol 2.2 (exploratory) applied Fisher's combination to the stored Study 2 p-values after those results were known: 63 of 64 suites flagged under the reduced spread and 5 of 64 clean suites. Part 3 repeats the comparison on new seeds with the method declared first.
part_3_suite_questions.conditions: The four conditions of protocol 2.0 covariance_study.conditions, in the order of condition_ids.
part_3_suite_questions.suites_justification: shared.evaluation_cases_per_condition: 93 suites give Wilson half-widths of at most 10 points for every suite-level rate.
part_3_suite_questions.check: timegym.diagnostics.covariance_dependence_check(case.reference, ensemble, seed=case seed + 2000000, n_calibration=239, alpha=0.05), exactly as experiments.run_supplement.run_covariance_study calls it.

questions.any_failure: Fisher's combination of the four p-values of a suite and variant: X = -2 sum log p against the chi-square law with 8 degrees of freedom (experiments.run_addendum.fisher_combination); the suite is flagged when the probability is <= 0.05. Valid because the four checks use independent seeds and each p-value is valid; discrete valid p-values make it conservative.
questions.which_condition: Holm at 0.05 over the four checks of a suite and variant (experiments.run_supplement.holm_rejections).

part_3_suite_questions.true_nulls: All four conditions in the clean variant; factorized_white_noise under the partial shuffle (negative control); none under the reduced spread.
reported: Per variant: suites flagged by Fisher, suites with any Holm rejection, suites with any raw rejection, with Wilson intervals.
Per variant: suites rejecting a true null under each method. Fisher's combination tests that all four nulls of a suite hold, so its count is reported for the clean variant only.
Per condition and variant: raw and Holm rejections with Wilson intervals.

part_4_joint_spread_margin.question: With what probability does a margin-based joint-spread decision return FAIL, WITHIN_TOLERANCE or INCONCLUSIVE when the true relative distance lies below, at or above the margin?
part_4_joint_spread_margin.location: experiments/study3_margin.py; not added to the package.

statistic.target: D = ||Sigma - Sigma0||_F / ||Sigma0||_F, the relative Frobenius distance of covariance_dependence_check, with Sigma the covariance of the ensemble's sample paths (horizon and targets flattened in C order) and Sigma0 the reference covariance.
statistic.estimator_of_D_squared: T = (tr_hat(Sigma^2) - 2 tr(S Sigma0) + tr(Sigma0^2)) / ||Sigma0||_F^2, with S the unbiased sample covariance (denominator n - 1) and tr_hat(Sigma^2) = Y1 - 2 Y2 + Y3, where Y1 averages (X_i'X_j)^2 over ordered pairs of distinct paths, Y2 averages (X_i'X_j)(X_j'X_k) over ordered triples of distinct paths, and Y3 averages (X_i'X_j)(X_k'X_l) over ordered quadruples of distinct paths; computed from the Gram matrix in O(n^2 p).
statistic.unbiasedness: E[T] = D^2 for independent paths with any common mean and finite fourth moments: tr_hat(Sigma^2) is unbiased for tr(Sigma^2) and tr(S Sigma0) for tr(Sigma Sigma0). Checked before registration by brute force and by Monte Carlo on a known case (pilots formula-checks).
statistic.citations: Cai and Ma (2013), Bernoulli 19(5B):2359-2388, doi 10.3150/12-bej455, Section 3.1, equations (6) and (7): for mean-zero Gaussian samples, the U-statistic with kernel h(X1, X2) = (X1'X2)^2 - (X1'X1 + X2'X2) + p is unbiased for ||Sigma - I||_F^2, and the test built on it is rate optimal when p/n is bounded. The general-target, unknown-mean form above extends that kernel; the tr(Sigma^2) estimator with unknown mean is the one of Chen, Zhang and Zhong (2010), JASA 105:810-819, doi 10.1198/jasa.2010.tm09560, which Cai and Ma cite as their reference [7]. Only Crossref metadata of Chen, Zhang and Zhong was reachable; the formula registered here was verified independently.

decision.standard_error: The leave-one-out (jackknife) standard error of T: with T_(i) the estimator recomputed without path i and T_bar the mean of the n values, se^2 = ((n - 1) / n) sum_i (T_(i) - T_bar)^2.
decision.interval: For D^2: from T - z se to T + z se with z = 1.6448536, the 95th percentile of the standard normal law. This is a two-sided 90% interval, so that each one-sided verdict is a claim at level 0.05, as in the two one-sided tests procedure (Schuirmann 1987, doi 10.1007/BF01068419). The interval reported for D takes the square roots of its ends, with a negative end set to 0.
decision.verdict: FAIL when T - z se is greater than the squared margin; WITHIN_TOLERANCE when T + z se is less than the squared margin; INCONCLUSIVE otherwise, including equality.
decision.justification: A bootstrap over the paths, the first design, is not used: a resample pairs a path with its own copy, which moves the centre of T upward by about ((tr Sigma)^2 + tr(Sigma^2)) / (n ||Sigma0||_F^2), measured as 0.205 at 64 paths on an identity covariance of dimension 12 (pilots resampling-formula-check), more than either squared margin. The jackknife leaves paths out and adds none. Its variance estimate is biased upward in expectation (Efron and Stein 1981, doi 10.1214/aos/1176345462), which pushes toward INCONCLUSIVE and away from both one-sided verdicts, and it is consistent for a U-statistic with a normal limit (Arvesen 1969, doi 10.1214/aoms/1177697287), the case D > 0. The normal quantile is an approximation at 64 and 256 paths; this simulation measures its error. The decision uses no random numbers.

margins.justification: 0.25 is a stricter tolerance; 0.4375 = |0.75^2 - 1| is the exact relative distance of the Study 2 spread multiplier 0.75 (verified in rational arithmetic), so that the Study 2 reduced spread sits exactly on the margin.

part_4_joint_spread_margin.conditions: The four Part 3 covariance conditions, in the order of part_3_suite_questions.condition_ids (reference covariance of dimension 12 = 6 steps x 2 targets).
part_4_joint_spread_margin.ensemble_construction: For a true distance d: spread multiplier c = sqrt(1 - d) (shrink) or c = sqrt(1 + d) (inflate); paths = reference.mean + c (Z - reference.mean) with Z the n draws case.reference.sample(n, seed) from the condition's exact conditional law, seed = int(numpy.random.SeedSequence([12000000, j, r]).generate_state(1)[0]), on the case generated with seed 12100000 + condition index (one fixed case per condition). Then Sigma = c^2 Sigma0 exactly and D = |c^2 - 1| = d. Only proportional departures from the reference covariance are simulated.

distance_grid.directions: Each nonzero distance in both directions (shrink and inflate); d = 0 once. 15 distances per margin.
distance_grid.justification: Dense around the margin, where the verdict rates change, with one point at half and one at 1.5 times the margin; the largest shrink, 1.5 x 0.4375 = 0.656, needs c = sqrt(1 - 0.65625) = 0.586.

repetitions.precision_target: Wilson 95% half-width at most 5 percentage points at any rate (381 is the smallest n meeting it).
repetitions.justification: The rate at d = margin is a level to be compared with 5%; 93 repetitions could not tell 5% from 12%. The simulation costs about 1.5 CPU-hours at 381.

part_4_joint_spread_margin.cells: 4 conditions x 2 margins x 15 distances x 2 path counts = 240 cells, indexed j from 0 in that nesting order: conditions in the order of part_3_suite_questions.condition_ids, margins 0.25 then 0.4375, the 15 distances of a margin as d = 0 first and then each nonzero multiple in increasing order with the shrink before the inflation, and 64 paths before 256.
reported: For every cell: counts and Wilson intervals of FAIL, WITHIN_TOLERANCE and INCONCLUSIVE.
The mean of T against d^2 per cell, as a check of unbiasedness.
part_4_joint_spread_margin.expectations_written_before_run: From the Gaussian variance of the estimator (Cai and Ma 2013, equation (9), with Sigma - Sigma0 in place of Sigma - I: 4 (tr^2(Sigma^2) + tr(Sigma^4)) / (n (n - 1)) + 8 tr((Sigma (Sigma - Sigma0))^2) / n, in units of ||Sigma0||_F^4), not from a simulation. At d = 0 and d = 0.5 margin the verdict is mostly WITHIN_TOLERANCE for the margin 0.4375 at both path counts and for the margin 0.25 at 256 paths; at 64 paths and the margin 0.25 INCONCLUSIVE is the most frequent verdict even at d = 0. At d = margin each of FAIL and WITHIN_TOLERANCE occurs in at most about 5% of repetitions, and in fewer where the jackknife overstates the variance. Above the margin FAIL grows with d and with the number of paths. At equal distance an inflated spread is harder to decide than a shrunken one, because the variance of the estimator grows with the spread of the ensemble.

part_5_predictability_estimators.question: How close do two published model-free predictability estimators come to the exact unavoidable error that the answer key provides?
part_5_predictability_estimators.cells: The 20 default scorecard cells: timegym.grid.scenario_grid() (ten patterns, noise sd 0.5 and 2.0, context 120, horizon 24).
part_5_predictability_estimators.series_justification: 200 matches the number of series behind each attainable mark (timegym.scorecard._ATTAINABLE_SERIES), enough to state a median and a 5 to 95 percentile range of a per-series ratio.
part_5_predictability_estimators.exact_floor: Per series: mean over the 24 horizon steps of case.reference.variance, the unavoidable error of the scorecard (timegym.scorecard._case_numbers).

spectral_bound.source: Feng, Yuan, Ding and Li, arXiv 2509.23074v3, Algorithm 1 and Appendix A.4.
spectral_bound.inputs: As the paper defines it, the bound needs a history segment x and the realized future segment y of equal length N: x = the last 24 context values, y = case.observed (the 24 realized values), N = 24. It is not an estimate from the history alone.
steps: Delta^2 = (mean(y) - mean(x))^2; the mean of each segment is then removed once.

Welch windows of length floor(0.25 N) = 6 with 50% overlap, starting at 0, 3, ..., 18: seven windows per segment, paired by position between x and y. Each window is multiplied by the periodic Hann window scipy.signal.windows.hann(6, sym=False) and transformed with numpy.fft.rfft (frequencies 0, 1/6, 1/3 and 1/2); windows are not detrended separately.
S_xx(f) and S_yy(f) are the means over the seven windows of |X_k(f)|^2 / U and |Y_k(f)|^2 / U, and S_xy(f) the mean of X_k(f) conj(Y_k(f)) / U, with U the sum of the squared window weights.
gamma^2(f) = |S_xy(f)|^2 / ((S_xx(f) + epsilon)(S_yy(f) + epsilon)), clipped to [0, 1], with epsilon = 1e-8.

MSE_lb = Delta^2 + V (1 - sum_f S_yy(f) gamma^2(f) / sum_f S_yy(f)), with V the sample variance of y with denominator N. This is the paper's Delta^2 + sum_f S_e(f) under its normalization sum_f S_yy(f) = V (equation 6).
spectral_bound.undefined: MSE_lb is undefined when V = 0 or sum_f S_yy(f) = 0 (a constant future segment), and the ratio MSE_lb / exact floor is also undefined when the exact floor is 0. Such series are recorded with a null value, counted per cell and for each of the two inputs, and left out of that cell's median and percentiles.
spectral_bound.constants_not_in_the_paper: The paper gives neither epsilon nor the Hann convention. epsilon = 1e-8 is the value in the authors' code (pilots authors-code-spectral-bound); the periodic Hann window is the convention of Welch routines and of one of that code's two paths.
spectral_bound.difference_from_the_authors_code: The authors' code never uses a Welch window shorter than 32 points, so at N = 24 it would use one window, give a coherence of 1 at every frequency and return Delta^2 alone. This protocol follows the paper's text (a window of floor(0.25 N)); the code's value is not computed.
spectral_bound.secondary_history_only: Also computed, and reported in its own columns: the same procedure with x = context values 73 to 96 and y = context values 97 to 120 (1-based), which uses the history alone.

permutation_entropy.source: Weighted permutation entropy as defined by Garland, James and Bradley (2014), Section V (arXiv 1404.6823v2), used for intrinsic predictability by Pennekamp et al. (2019).
permutation_entropy.definition: For word length l and delay 1 over the 120 context values: each window of l consecutive values gets its ordinal pattern and the weight w = (1/l) sum (x_j - window mean)^2; P_w(pi) = sum of weights of windows with pattern pi divided by the sum of all weights; WPE = -sum P_w(pi) log2 P_w(pi) / log2(l!).
permutation_entropy.ties: Ordinal patterns come from a stable sort, so equal values rank in order of occurrence.
permutation_entropy.parameters: Garland et al.'s rule l = argmax{N >= 100 l!} admits no l >= 2 at N = 120 (l = 3 would need 600 values). l = 3 is the smallest length in the range 3 to 6 that they call standard, and leaves 118 windows for 6 patterns. The parameters used by Pennekamp et al. (2019) were not checked, because their text was not reachable.
permutation_entropy.undefined: WPE is undefined when every window has weight zero (a constant context). Such series are recorded with a null value, counted per cell and left out of the cell's median.

part_5_predictability_estimators.table: One row per cell: median and 5th to 95th percentile (numpy.percentile, linear interpolation) of MSE_lb / exact floor over the series where it is defined, for the primary inputs and for the history-only inputs; the number of series where each ratio is undefined; median WPE and the number of series where it is undefined; the row's exact floor, which is the median over its 200 series of the per-series exact floor; and the row's scale-free floor, the median over its series of the exact floor divided by the variance of the 120 context values (denominator 120). The two random-walk rows are labelled as having no stationary spectrum. Below the table: the Spearman rank correlation (scipy.stats.spearmanr, average ranks for ties) across the 20 rows between median WPE and the row's exact floor. Twelve of the 20 rows share one of two floor values (the noise variances 0.25 and 4.0), so that correlation mostly separates the two noise levels, and WPE does not depend on scale; a second correlation is therefore reported, between median WPE and the row's scale-free floor.
part_5_predictability_estimators.expectations_written_before_run: Spectral bound over exact floor, primary inputs. Close to 1 on the stationary rows (pure noise, noise around a fixed level, mean reversion, irregular cycles): a median between 0.5 and 1.5, and a little below 1 on the first two, because the coherence of two unrelated segments estimated from seven overlapping windows is positive on average. Off on straight-line trend, repeating seasonal cycle, trend plus seasonal cycle and sudden level shift, where the predictable part is deterministic; above 1 on the two trend rows, where the mean term Delta^2 dominates. On the two random-walk rows the bound is not defined in theory (no stationary spectrum); its values are reported and labelled so. Weighted permutation entropy is highest on the pure-noise and fixed-level rows, and its rank correlation with the scale-free floor is positive.
part_5_predictability_estimators.restriction: Neither estimator was run on any scorecard cell before registration.

part_6_zoo.question: What scorecards do commonly used forecasting models get on the default grid, beside each row's attainable mark?
part_6_zoo.location: experiments/zoo/ with its own lock files; no dependency enters the package or the study lock.
part_6_zoo.scorecard: Pipeline(model).scorecard(seed=14000000, instances=30) with every other argument at its default (ten patterns, two noise levels, context 120, horizon 24); the attainable mark is the stored one of timegym.scorecard._ATTAINABLE.

chronos-forecasting 2.3.2, ChronosPipeline.from_pretrained('amazon/chronos-t5-small', revision=<the revision field of this entry, see pretrained_revision>, device_map='cpu', torch_dtype=float32); 100 sample paths per forecast (the package default is 20), so that the Monte Carlo error of the sample mean adds about 1% to the squared error instead of 5%; the forecast carries the samples and point = their mean.

experiments/zoo/parroting.py, NumPy only, Algorithm 1 of Zhang and Gilpin (arXiv 2505.11349v3): with embedding dimension D = 10 (the value of the paper's Figure 5; it also uses 5 and reports little sensitivity), find the length-D motif in x_1..x_(L-D) nearest in Euclidean distance to the last D values (candidate motifs start at s = 1, ..., L - 2D + 1), and copy the values that followed it, x_(s+D)..x_L, repeating that copy from its start until 24 values. Each target is forecast alone. Ties go to the earliest motif, a convention of this protocol. Deterministic; no training.

part_6_zoo.hyperparameters: Fixed for every row; no per-row tuning. season_length 12 is the grid's seasonal period.
part_6_zoo.figure: One figure: rows the ten patterns, columns the nine models in the order of models; each cell shows the low-noise and high-noise scores with their intervals (the scorecard's score_low and score_high, as the package computes them at the registered commit) beside the row's attainable mark. It is drawn from the saved files alone. No ranking claim is made and no model is ordered by score.
part_6_zoo.declared_overlap: Chronos was pretrained on real datasets, TSMixup combinations of them, and KernelSynth series drawn from Gaussian processes whose kernels combine Constant, White Noise, Linear, RBF, Rational Quadratic and Periodic kernels (periods including 12), by sum or product (arXiv 2403.07815, Table 2). Rows resembling that synthetic data: pure noise, fixed level, straight-line trend, repeating seasonal cycle (period 12) and trend plus seasonal cycle. Partly: irregular cycles (a Periodic times RBF composition is quasi-periodic). Not in the kernel bank: sudden level shift, mean reversion (an exponential kernel is not in the bank), random walk and random walk with drift. The overlap with the real pretraining data cannot be stated.
part_6_zoo.pretrained_revision: The commit hash of amazon/chronos-t5-small could not be read when this protocol was drafted (the model host was not reachable). It is written into the revision field of the chronos_small entry of models, which is null until then, before the Chronos scorecard runs, by a commit that changes only that value, and the manifest must show the same hash. The other eight scorecards do not depend on it.
part_6_zoo.pretrained_environment: The Chronos scorecard may run on another machine. It installs experiments/zoo/requirements-chronos.txt with a CPU-only torch, sets torch.set_num_threads(1), and records in its manifest: Python version, platform string, CPU model, pip freeze, torch.__version__ and torch.__config__.show(), the Hugging Face model id, the resolved commit hash (which must equal the registered one), the SHA-256 of every downloaded weight and configuration file, and the timegym commit. Its scorecard baseline (Scorecard.save_baseline) and manifest are committed to experiments/results-v3/zoo/ beside the others; the figure is drawn from the saved baselines.
part_6_zoo.runtime_estimate: About 20 minutes here for the eight local models (600 series each; AutoARIMA about 1 s per series); Chronos on one CPU thread is expected to take tens of minutes; not timed, because the weights were not reachable.
part_6_zoo.prior_scorecards: Scorecards of the two built-in baselines and of a Ridge lag pipeline on the default grid at other seeds are in the paper and the documentation, and the last-value forecaster was scored on other seeds again, on 14 and on 16 November 2026, when the scorecard's interval was measured and then changed (pilots_before_registration, earlier-exploratory-records). The other seven models have not been scored.
part_6_zoo.outputs: Four files per model in experiments/results-v3/zoo/: <model id>.json (Scorecard.save_baseline), <model id>.table.csv (per cell: score, score_low, score_high, attainable, instances, failed_checks), <model id>.manifest.json (protocol digest, digests of the two files and of the zoo's sources, seeds, library versions, and for Chronos what pretrained_environment lists) and <model id>.runtime.json (wall time and thread pools). A model's existing files are refused unless --force.
